responsibility: This module is GCC’s PowerPC/RS6000 target backend, responsible for turning GCC’s generic IR into code, ABI behavior, and user-visible target interfaces for the broad Power/PowerPC family across AIX/XCOFF, ELF System V, Linux, Darwin, BSD, RTEMS, VxWorks, and embedded environments. Its core rs6000.{cc,h,md,opt} files define target hooks, option state, register and mode rules, instruction patterns, and overall ISA/ABI policy; call-, prologue/epilogue-, and string-expansion files implement PowerPC calling conventions, stack frame generation, save/restore logic, and efficient block-memory lowering; builtin definition/generation and front-end hook files provide AltiVec, VSX, HTM, MMA, paired-single, CPU-query, and language-specific builtin support together with public intrinsic headers; numerous subtarget headers specialize object format, linker/driver specs, defaults, and OS ABI details; processor-specific .md families supply scheduler models and instruction-set extensions for many POWER, embedded e* cores, Cell, Xilinx, and future CPUs; and target-only RTL passes such as Power8 swap cleanup and PC-relative access optimization refine generated code for Power-specific execution and relocation behavior. Overall, this directory is the complete machine-dependent implementation that distinguishes GCC’s PowerPC/RS6000 code generation, tuning, diagnostics, and platform integration from neighboring target backends.
